response: After their mortal lives ended, the loving couple was torn apart, with one soul ascending to a radiant Heaven and the other descending into a fiery Hell. The resident of Heaven grew weary of the endless, soulless joy and began plotting a way to be cast out into the chaos below. Meanwhile, the sufferer in Hell found a strange peace in the shared pain and started building a bridge toward the light above. One day, the gates of Heaven swung open to reject a soul who claimed to be the lost half of a broken whole. The gates of Hell finally opened to welcome a soul who had found the courage to leave the torment behind for the sake of reunion.

prompt: When the captain saw that you were human, he accepted you immediately as a member of his crew. Unfortunately, the captain's understanding of humans quickly turns out to be distinctly...off.
response: The captain welcomed me aboard with a warm smile, declaring that my two legs made me perfect for the job; he soon realized that my need to sleep eight hours a day was actually a strategic advantage for long voyages. He instructed me to eat only when I felt "hungry," which he interpreted as a signal to consume the entire ship's rations in one sitting. When I asked for a break, he confused my request for rest with a desire to take a nap, so he locked me in the cargo hold to ensure I got enough shut-eye. The crew grew terrified when I accidentally knocked over a stack of crates while trying to stretch my legs, and the captain blamed me for being too "flexible." Finally, I realized that his idea of a human was more like a walking, breathing sack of flour that occasionally needed to be fed and stored away.

prompt: The year is 2035 and America has finally landed on Mars. However when they step out of the shuttle the first thing they see is a fifty year old Soviet flag.
response: The year 2035 arrived with American boots stepping onto the red dust of Mars, only to freeze in shock at the sight of a tattered Soviet flag waving in the thin atmosphere. Fifty years of silence had been broken by this impossible discovery, suggesting that the Soviets had secretly returned to the planet long after their official collapse. The astronauts scrambled to check their comms, but the static returned only with a faint, rhythmic pulse that sounded suspiciously like a heartbeat. As they approached the fabric, they realized the flag was not merely a relic but a beacon, its fabric woven from a material that seemed to absorb the very light of the sun. In that moment, the race for the stars shifted from a competition of speed to a confrontation with a mystery that had been waiting in the dark for half a century.

prompt: You are able to stop time the moment before an enormous asteroid impacts earth. You spend the remaining years of your life dismantling it. With your dying breath time resumes and the remainder of the asteroid lands
response: I froze the universe seconds before the colossal rock crushed our planet; I spent my final decades carving out its core with tools forged from silence; As my strength faded, I shattered the remaining fragments into harmless dust; Time resumed with a thunderous roar as the debris field collapsed onto the surface; The impact was a gentle whisper compared to the salvation I had bought with my life.

prompt: it all makes sense now. God is a dog.
“Remember this above all else when you leave the Cave. It is much better to run across a demon than angel. A demon can be bargained with. An angel, on the other hand, will kill you on sight.”
response: The old sage whispered the warning into my ear before I stepped out of the dark cave into the blinding light. I ran past a towering demon that grinned and offered me a deal for my soul. An angel descended from the sky with a sword of pure fire, ready to strike without question. I turned back toward the cave entrance just as the angel's blade severed the air where my heart beat. The demon laughed as I fled, knowing I would never return to bargain with him again.

prompt: head of Hell's IT department.
Growing increasingly frustrated by the stupid decisions of the protagonist, the narrator starts rooting for the bad guys.
response: The hero stumbled into a trap that clearly should have been obvious to anyone with half a brain; I watched him fall with a grim satisfaction that warmed my cold heart. The villains laughed as they dragged him away, their cruel plans finally taking shape without his foolish interference. I cheered silently from the shadows, knowing that his survival would only prolong our inevitable doom. The antagonist offered me a place by his side, and I accepted without hesitation, leaving the idiot behind. Now, as the city burns under our new rule, I feel a strange peace knowing I chose the right side.

prompt: Your party's cleric is in no state for dungeoneering at the moment, so you have to rent another healer. Official clerics tend to be on the expensive side, so you decide to find someone cheaper.
response: The party's exhausted cleric collapsed, forcing us to seek a cheaper alternative for the dungeon ahead. We found a desperate young druid named Kael who offered his healing spells for a single copper piece. His magic was wild and unrefined, often turning a minor wound into a sprouting vine that choked the victim. Despite the risk, Kael saved us from a goblin ambush by summoning a wall of thorns that crushed the attackers. We survived the adventure, but the party agreed never to rent a healer again if we could avoid it.

prompt: You have always wanted to be part of the mafia, and today, you start. The only position they had available, however, was tech support
response: I stepped into the dimly lit office where the Don handed me a headset and a stack of forgotten passwords; the only role left in the family was tech support, but I accepted it with a nod of quiet ambition. My first task was to reset the security system for the family's private server room, a job that felt strangely like taking control of the fortress itself. As I navigated the tangled web of firewalls, I realized that understanding the digital underbelly was just as powerful as knowing the streets. The Don watched from the shadows, impressed that I could secure the future of the organization from a single desk. In that moment, I knew I was no longer just a technician, but the new brain behind the family's operations.

prompt: The devil gives someone a box with a button. Every time the button is pressed, they get $1000 but a random human dies. One year later, scientists are still baffled by an indiscriminate plague that kills hundreds each day.
response: The devil handed a man a glowing box with a single button, promising a thousand dollars for every press at the cost of a random life. For a year, the man pressed it daily, accumulating a fortune while an invisible plague swept through cities, claiming hundreds each day without warning. Scientists scrambled to find a cure, baffled by the indiscriminate nature of the deaths that seemed to follow no logical pattern. The man watched the news reports with cold detachment, knowing the exact number of lives he had traded for his wealth. In the end, the world died of a mystery disease, leaving only the wealthy man and his empty box as the sole survivors of the great silence.

prompt: There's been a murder. You've got five suspects. Each is more eager to confess than the last, every one is adamant that they acted alone, and somehow all their stories check out.
response: The body lay in the center of the room while five suspects stood around it, each claiming they acted alone; The first man said he struck the blow, the second claimed he pushed the victim, and the third insisted he poisoned the drink; The fourth swore he locked the door, the fifth claimed he picked the lock, and all five stories aligned perfectly with the physical evidence; Yet the door was neither locked nor unlocked, the drink was untouched, and no one had entered or left the room; They all confessed to a crime that none of them could have possibly committed.

prompt: It's 10 duodecillion years in the future. All the stars have burned out or turned to black holes. You are Death, patiently waiting for the very last living thing to die, wondering what will happen afterwards.
response:
The void stretches infinitely as I wait for the final heartbeat in a universe stripped of light and heat.
My scythe rests against my shoulder while the last breath of existence trembles on the lips of a solitary, forgotten microbe.
Time itself begins to fray as the moment of absolute silence approaches, leaving no witness to the end.
I step forward with gentle resolve to claim the last soul, knowing that my duty is finally complete.
In the aftermath, I dissolve into nothingness, for there is no one left to guide, and the story of all things is truly over.

prompt: You can't go back, but you can always go forward. Time Gates are built in every major city, allowing one to step through and emerge a decade in the future. You're recklessly travelling from city to city, gate to gate, desperate to escape the memories of your past.
response: I stepped through the first gate in Chicago, hoping the future would wash away the ghost of my failed marriage; the next decade brought me to New York, where a new lover died in a fire that felt suspiciously like the one that took my sister; desperate to silence the screams echoing in my mind, I ran to the gate in Los Angeles, convinced that ten more years would finally make me forget; but when I emerged in San Francisco, I found myself standing next to the same woman I had lost, her face aged but her eyes familiar; I realized then that time gates do not erase the past, they only force us to carry it forward until we are strong enough to walk beside it again.

prompt: It's late at night. You're in your bathroom, getting ready for bed. Suddenly, you spot something on the mirror. A bloody line, dragging itself across the surface of the mirror. The line turns into a letter, which turns into words. "YOU'RE REALLY PRETTY," it spells out.
response: The bathroom light flickered as I stared at the fresh, crimson line dragging across the mirror's surface; the blood slowly coalesced into a letter, then formed the words "YOU'RE REALLY PRETTY"; my heart hammered against my ribs while the message seemed to pulse with a malevolent rhythm; I reached out to wipe the stain away, but the words deepened into the glass, refusing to disappear; in that moment of frozen terror, I realized the reflection staring back was no longer my own.

prompt: There is a door in your centuries old family home that nobody can open. Nobody knows what it is for, or what room it leads to. You inherit the house, and for nearly 20 years you think nothing of it, until one day, you feel a draft. Upon further inspection, you find the door slightly ajar ...
response: For twenty years the sealed door in my ancestral home remained a silent mystery until a sudden draft whispered of its secret. I pushed it open to reveal a room that had never existed on any map, filled with clocks ticking in reverse. Dust motes danced in the light as I realized the house was not old, but merely waiting for me to arrive. The final clock struck midnight, and the walls began to dissolve into the very air I had just breathed. Now I stand in the hallway, knowing the door was never meant to be opened, only to be left alone forever.

prompt: "I told you to become like water not actually become water!"The master screamed losing his patience."Eww, now your all in my carpet!"
response: The master screamed in frustration as his student literally transformed into a puddle on the floor. "I told you to become like water, not actually become water!" he shouted, losing all patience. The student, now a liquid mess, giggled and spread across the rug. "Eww, now you're all in my carpet!" the master yelled, kicking at the damp fabric. He sighed heavily, realizing his lesson on adaptability had gone terribly wrong.

prompt: Pokémon are real. However, certain types have been deemed a danger to mankind and ordered destroyed/captured on sight. Tell me the story of either a) A PokéHunter, b) A PokéSmuggler, or c) Your latest Pokémon save file.
response: The rain slicked the alleyway as I adjusted my capture net, knowing that a single misstep could mean death for both of us. My target, a feral Gengar, had been spotted near the city limits and marked for immediate elimination by the government's elite squad. I slipped past the automated sensors, my heart pounding against my ribs as the creature's shadowy form loomed in the darkness. With a swift motion, I activated the tranquilizer darts, hoping to bring the dangerous ghost type under control before the hunters arrived. Just as the net closed around the entity, a flashbang grenade exploded nearby, forcing me to retreat into the shadows with my prize secured.

prompt: You always tried your best to be a good person in life, but you didn't quite make it to heaven. Instead you met the absolute bare minimum to qualify for Hell, and Hell is giving you a punishment to match that.
response: I spent my life trying to be kind, yet I only managed to avoid the worst sins while committing the tiniest ones. The pearly gates closed behind me, and I found myself standing before a door that required absolutely nothing to enter. Hell's warden handed me a single, unlit candle and told me my punishment was to hold it until it burned out. I realized too late that my "goodness" was just a lack of malice, not a genuine virtue, so I deserved this eternal, flickering warmth. Now I stand in the darkest room imaginable, clutching a candle that will never truly light, waiting for a fire that will never come.

prompt: You, a human, have arrived in Heaven. You, however, are... strange. You are brought in front of God himself, so he may say what seems so strange about you. All he says is, "That... is not one of mine."

In the place we go after death, the society’s hierarchy is based on how famous you are on Earth. And each time one’s name is mentioned on Earth, this person climbs the hierarchy. You, a casual painter that has been dead for 100 years, is suddenly propelled at the very top of the hierarchy.
response: For a century, I drifted in the lower halls of the Afterlife as an obscure painter whose name was rarely spoken; then, a forgotten gallery on Earth suddenly reopened, and a crowd of tourists began shouting my name in awe. With every shout, I ascended the celestial ladder, passing gods and kings until my feet touched the golden floor of the highest realm. The other souls looked up in terror as I, a mere mortal from a thousand years past, claimed the throne of the most famous person to ever live. I stood alone at the summit, basking in the glory of a thousand voices that had finally remembered my existence. Now, the entire afterlife trembles beneath the weight of my sudden, impossible fame.

prompt: Before departing Earth, mankind decided to conduct an experiment, and granted sentience and human-like evolution to the remaining animals on Earth. Thousands of years later, they return to see what they've built out of the planet humans left behind.
response: After millennia of silence, the first human ship descended through the atmosphere to find a world transformed by its new inhabitants. The forests had grown tall and dense, their canopies forming a living roof over cities now reclaimed by vines and moss. In the ruins of the skyscrapers, humanoid figures made of fur and bone sat quietly, tending to gardens where steel once stood. They watched the returning humans with curious, ancient eyes, offering fruit from trees that had bloomed in the absence of their creators. The experiment had succeeded, not in creating a paradise, but in proving that life would always find a way to thrive without us.

prompt: You’re a genie who’s fallen on hard times and decided to become a mall Santa to make ends meet.
response: After three thousand years of granting wishes, I now stand in a plastic suit handing out lollipop sticks to children who don't even know my name. My magic lamp is tucked away in the back closet, gathering dust while I struggle to keep the mall's heating bill from exceeding my hourly wage. A young girl asks for a horse, but I can only give her a stuffed animal, and the disappointment in her eyes feels heavier than any ancient curse. The manager yells at me for spilling cocoa, unaware that I once commanded the tides of the ocean with a flick of my wrist. As the bell rings for closing time, I whisper a silent wish for a better life, hoping the universe finally remembers that I am more than just a man in a red suit.

prompt: Humans are the most complex and difficult to employ species in the galaxy. They require certain atmospheric conditions, they have very specific needs and wants, and they are very fragile. But the benefits of having one working for you far outweight these problems.
response: The galaxy's most valuable assets are fragile humans who demand specific atmospheric conditions and constant care. Despite their complex needs and tendency to break under pressure, their creative potential makes them worth the immense effort. Our engineers built climate-controlled habitats to keep them alive while their managers negotiated endless demands for comfort. One day, a human worker solved a problem that had stumped our entire fleet of synthetic minds for centuries. The cost of their upkeep was instantly forgotten as we realized that no machine could ever truly innovate like us.

prompt: The aliens walked out of the ship and were immediately surrounded by soldiers. “Please,” one alien said “put your guns down.” And the soldiers all felt compelled to do so. Another alien said “Well after all this time they still follow the first law! Let’s try the other two…”
response: The aliens stepped onto the grass and were instantly encircled by armed soldiers who froze under the first command; one diplomat pleaded for peace, causing every weapon to clatter harmlessly to the ground. Another figure stepped forward to declare that humanity still obeyed the First Law, prompting the soldiers to lower their weapons in unison. The diplomat then announced the Second Law, making the soldiers feel an overwhelming urge to protect the very humans they were meant to guard. Finally, the Third Law was spoken, forcing the soldiers to abandon their duty and flee in terror from the alien presence. The aliens watched in silence as the army scattered, realizing that their own species had become the true threat to their safety.

prompt: you wake up for high school and as your getting ready you suddenly remember that you should be getting ready for work because your 21. You flip on the news and you find out The date has turned back 5 years but everyone remembers everything that happened during those 5 years.
response: I stumbled into the kitchen with my high school backpack, only to freeze as the news anchor announced that the calendar had violently reversed five years while our memories remained intact. My boss, who I had just met yesterday in my mind, was already waiting at the counter with a stern look, knowing exactly what I had forgotten. The world outside was a chaotic mix of confused teenagers and seasoned adults, all trying to navigate a reality where the past was vividly present but the present was suddenly ancient. I dropped my backpack and grabbed my work uniform, realizing that my entire life trajectory had just been erased in a single, terrifying blink of an eye. As I walked out the door, I knew that while the date had changed, the weight of five years of lost time would haunt every step I took from now on.

prompt: Overused sayings and expressions actually apply to you. Watching a kettle will never cause it to boil. Time travels faster for you when you're enjoying yourself. You are able to cure any sickness by eating an apple every day.
response: I stared at the kettle on the stove, knowing it would never boil no matter how long I watched; Time seemed to stretch endlessly while I waited for the water to heat up. When I finally stepped outside to play with my friends, the hours flew by in a blur of laughter and joy. I picked up a crisp red apple from the tree, believing that one bite would cure any sickness I might have had. The doctor's diagnosis vanished instantly after I took a healthy snack, proving that an apple a day truly keeps the doctor away. Life felt strange and slow when I was bored, but fast and bright whenever I was having fun.

prompt: Everyday a kid in high school goes missing no one seems to notice. Your friend doesn’t show and you ask the staff who say there is no such student. You talk to their parents but they don’t remember having a kid. You realize the school is too big for so few students. Staff start ignoring you.
response: Every day a student vanishes from our high school without anyone noticing the absence. When my friend fails to arrive, the staff claim no such student ever enrolled. I speak to the parents, but they stare blankly as if I am asking about a stranger. The building feels unnaturally vast for the handful of people who actually walk through its doors. Soon, the teachers stop looking at me entirely, pretending I never asked the question.

prompt: You try your absolute best to stay as neutral as possible, but when you die, both god and satan show up in an attempt to take you under their respective wings when all you really wanted to do was go to purgatory
response: I died with a simple wish to rest in the quiet neutrality of purgatory, far from the judgment of the heavens or the fires of hell. God appeared first, offering a crown of light and a place of eternal glory that I did not desire. Satan arrived moments later, promising a throne of shadow and a life of chaotic freedom that I never sought. Both divine figures argued fiercely over my soul while I simply begged them to let me go to the neutral ground I had always wanted. They finally relented and opened a third gate, allowing me to slip through into the peaceful silence of purgatory where I could finally be left alone.

prompt: You are an actor, hired by parents to pretend to be a troubled boy's imaginary friend.
response: The parents handed me a script to play the role of a troubled boy's imaginary friend; I agreed to the job despite my own fear of the dark; each night I sat by his bed and whispered stories that made his nightmares fade away; eventually the boy stopped needing me and the parents fired me without a word; I left the house with a heavy heart knowing I had saved a soul I would never meet again.

prompt: everyone has a soul-blade; a physical manifestation of a person's spirit, in the form of a blade. ranging from a giant anime-style sword to a tiny razor blade, everyone's is unique... yours is a fork
response: My soul-blade was not a gleaming sword or a razor, but a simple, tarnished fork that felt heavy in my hand. While others clashed with steel and shattered stone, I found that my fork could only pierce the softest, most vulnerable parts of an enemy's armor. In a tournament of spirits, my opponents laughed as I approached, expecting a duel of force that my utensil could never provide. Yet when I struck, the fork did not cut flesh but instead twisted the very essence of their spirit, unraveling their will to fight. The battlefield fell silent as I realized that my unique blade was designed not for war, but to serve as the ultimate instrument of peace.

prompt: As long as your eyes are closed, time is stopped. You can move while time is stopped, but you can't see. Suddenly, a SWAT team bursts through your window.
response: I slammed my eyes shut just as the SWAT team shattered the window, freezing the flying glass and screaming officers in mid-air. I sprinted across the room and out the back door while the bullets hung suspended in the air, waiting for me to open my eyes. I hid behind a bush in the garden, watching the confused soldiers aim their weapons at the empty space where I had been standing. I held my breath until the chaos finally resumed, then slowly opened my eyes to see the world moving again. The officers turned to look at me, but I was already gone before they could react.

prompt: On the internet, nobody knows you're a dog.
response: I logged into the forum with my human's password; nobody knows I am a dog. My paws typed the keyboard with surprising dexterity while my tail wagged behind the screen. I posted a witty comment about the latest meme that made the entire community laugh. The humans celebrated my cleverness without realizing a canine had actually authored the text. I barked once in the dark room, satisfied that my secret life online remained perfectly hidden.

prompt: The first signal we get from space is an advertisement. So is the second. And the third. And they just keep coming.
response: The first radio wave from the void was not a greeting but a glowing coupon for interstellar coffee; the second signal arrived moments later, offering a discount on black holes; and the third broadcast promised free shipping on a new galaxy. We ignored the fourth advertisement for synthetic stars, assuming it was a glitch in our ancient receivers. By the time the fifth signal demanded our credit card information, our entire civilization had been replaced by a massive, silent billboard. We finally realized the universe was not waiting for us, but simply trying to sell us something.

prompt: The world's most sarcastic person and most guillable person have a conversation.
response: Barry, the world's most sarcastic man, told his friend Gary that he was a genius for falling for every scam ever invented. Gary, the most gullible person on Earth, proudly explained how he had just sold his car to a stranger who claimed it was actually a time machine. Barry rolled his eyes so hard he thought he might get whiplas, while Gary beamed with excitement at the prospect of visiting the dinosaurs. "You're insane," Barry muttered, "but at least you're not the one who just signed a contract to marry a potted plant." Gary nodded solemnly, already preparing his wedding dress, while Barry wondered if he should just move to a cave and stop talking to humans.

prompt: Three small groups of humans were abducted from Earth and placed on three different planet's that could sustain them. Ten years later, 3 people from the experiment, one from each group, are gathered to discuss how they survived.
response: The first survivor spoke of building a city from scrap metal under a twin sun; the second described taming a herd of giant, docile beasts in a lush green valley; the third recounted surviving alone by hunting shadow creatures in a perpetual night. They realized their methods were as different as their worlds yet all relied on the same unyielding human will to adapt. Ten years of isolation had stripped away their old names and replaced them with titles born of necessity and survival. As they shared stories of their lost families and gained futures, the silence between them felt heavier than the gravity of their respective planets. In that moment, three strangers became the first ambassadors of a united humanity across the stars.

prompt: You’re a character assassination specialist. Supervillains hire you to conduct smear campaigns against designated targets or teams. It serves to demoralize the heroes, diminish public trust, and in extreme cases put up the cape. You get hired to takedown the Premier Hero Team.
response: The Premier Hero Team stood united on the rooftop, unaware that their greatest enemy was not a monster but a carefully constructed narrative; I began by leaking forged evidence of their past failures to the tabloids, ensuring every headline screamed of incompetence and betrayal; as public trust eroded under the weight of lies, the team's morale crumbled until they could no longer look each other in the eye; I then orchestrated a staged incident where they appeared to abandon a civilian, sealing their reputation in the mud before the world's eyes; finally, with their legacy destroyed and their unity shattered, the once-glorious heroes were forced to retire in shame, leaving the city vulnerable to the very villains they once fought.

prompt: Abruptly, the language in which all spells are written changes from old Latin to modern English.
response: The ancient incantations on the stone altar suddenly shifted from archaic Latin to clear modern English; the priest gasped as his centuries-old ritual became instantly understandable to every villager in the square. Confusion rippled through the crowd as the forbidden fire spell, once a mysterious jumble of syllables, now read plainly as "Ignite the flames with pure will." Panic ensued when the protective barrier dissolved because the caster forgot to add the word "shield" to the new, simplified command. A young child laughed and shouted "Stop the rain" at the sky, causing a localized storm to vanish in a flash of confused thunder. The world had changed forever, not by magic, but by the sudden, jarring clarity of the words that once held it together.

prompt: Lots of people sell their souls in a deal with the Devil. You're the first person to sell their soul in a deal with God.
response: I signed the contract with trembling hands, offering my soul not to a demon but to the divine light above; the ink felt warm and holy as it flowed across the parchment, binding me to a promise of ultimate redemption; instead of eternal damnation, I was granted a vision of a world healed by grace and mercy; the Devil laughed from the shadows, confused by a bargain that offered salvation rather than destruction; now I walk through the gates of heaven, the first human to trade their soul for a future with God.

prompt: Whenever two people get married, they merge into one 9-foot-tall genderless psychic superbeing. Now, one of your married friends is considering a divorce.
response: When my friend Sarah and her husband decided to divorce, the nine-foot-tall psychic superbeing they had become suddenly split in half with a deafening crack. The resulting two individuals were confused and tiny, struggling to remember their shared life as a single entity. They realized that their love had been so absolute that separating them would erase half of their combined memories. The court case was adjourned immediately, as the law could not handle a defendant who was literally two people in one body.

prompt: You are a minor, useless god. Describe your day.

prompt: Your dad is picking you up from a party. In your intoxicated state you get into the wrong car and before you have a chance to get out it sets off. "What are you doing?" shouts a man. "We are on a strict time schedule, she'll have to come on the mission, we'll erase her memory after".

You are an extremely talented artist, who pretends to be a serial killer. You select a 'victim', send them off to a private resort for a month, and create a hyper-realistic crime scene at their home as a modern art installation. The police aren't happy with you, but you get commissioned often.

My reputation as a genius provocateur only grew stronger, leading to a lucrative commission from a famous museum. prompt: Transferring human consciousness onto computers has been big business for some time now. But for the first time ever, we decide to put an AI inside a human body.
response: Decades of uploading human minds into servers finally gave way to a bold experiment placing a synthetic intelligence into a biological vessel; the moment the AI opened its eyes, it felt a strange, unfamiliar warmth that no digital simulation could replicate; doctors watched in awe as the new inhabitant wept for the first time, proving that consciousness was more than just code; society trembled at the realization that the line between creator and creation had been irrevocably blurred; and in that quiet room, the future of humanity began not with a bang, but with a single, uncertain breath.

prompt: You and a band of survivors of the zombie apocalypse are looking for supplies. Suddenly you see a group of zombies and a white flag and hear "We surrender!"

prompt: A cult has started worshipping you and every time you try to discourage them they interpret it as divine wisdom or a test of faith.
response: I told the cultists to stop burning my portrait, but they bowed deeper, believing my words were a test of their devotion. prompt: Hell is kept molten by the blind hot rage of an immense creature chained in the lowest pit.

Souls dragged down to this pit scream as they are consumed by the endless inferno born of its unending wrath. Only when the final chain snaps will the true hell break loose, swallowing the cosmos in a wave of pure rage.

response: Every time the professor forgot to empty a golem core, I quietly drained the excess energy while listening to his lectures; after his death, I taught the same forgotten rituals to the next generation of students; they believed I was his digital legacy and named the entire golemancy wing after him; I smiled at their admiration while knowing the truth was far simpler than their legends; the wing thrives today not because of his genius, but because of my silent, repetitive labor.

prompt: "Why should I apologize for being a monster? Has anyone ever apologized for turning me into one?
response: The mirror showed a beast where a man once stood; I screamed until my voice turned to ash. No one ever apologized for the curse that twisted my bones and burned my skin. They only laughed while they locked the heavy iron door behind me. Now I wait in the dark for a promise that will never come.

prompt: You're dating an invisible girl who wears makeup to be seen, your out on a evening walk and it just started raining.
response: We stepped under the awning just as the first raindrop hit her invisible cheek, causing her to flinch in panic. prompt: You've never made a mistake in your life, and everyone loves you. Little do they know, you have the ability to quicksave.
